title: Under default role mode X-Role: __union__ is silently rewritten to the user's first role instead of being refused
statement: Every role name a user does not hold is refused with 401 ROLE_NOT_FOUND_FOR_USER. The single exception is __union__ under the default role mode: setCurrentRole rewrites it to userRoles[0] and rewrites the request header too, so the request runs as a role the caller never named and answers 200. The caller cannot tell from the response that a substitution happened.

handVerified.note: Report section 7. Two-role user tcunion: the __union__ answer is byte-identical to the tcuniona answer (3 rows, no sex column). Control 1: X-Role: admin and X-Role: tcnosuchrole both 401. Control 2: flipping to allow-use-union and re-issuing the SAME request returns 4 rows with both age and sex, which proves the default-mode answer was one role's answer and not a union that happened to look like it. No F-number in findings.md; tracked as run-classification.md section 9.6 and board row 13.

source.howDecided: git log d8d8cb4b..origin/main -- <culprit files> returned 0 commits for every file in this finding. The only three commits since the tested SHA are 24a620efb8 and 032a4f6913 (lerna version bumps, packages/*/package.json and lerna.json only) and ba00bcebc2 (CHANGELOG.md, CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md). The culprit lines were then re-read at origin/main and match the report's quotes.

citedItems.note: fix(plugin-acl): preserve union default role members. Predates the tested SHA and does not touch the rewrite branch.
roles union variable in v2; unrelated code fix, predates the tested SHA.

reevaluation: The finding stands unchanged. setCurrentRole.ts has no commit since the tested SHA; lines 55-58 still rewrite currentRole, ctx.state.currentRole and ctx.headers['x-role'] to userRoles[0].name, and lines 74-81 still 401 every other unheld name. UNION_ROLE_KEY is still '__union__' at constants.ts:10. The __union__ symptom search returned only #9632 (already cited, unchanged) and an unrelated LDAP regression, so nothing new. One scope point a filer must get right: the substituted role is one the caller DOES hold, so this is not a privilege escalation. It is a silent substitution where the same middleware refuses every comparable input.
notes: Do NOT file this as a security issue and do not imply escalation: userRoles[0] is always a role the caller holds, so the effective permissions are a subset of the union the caller asked for. The report's Control 2 (same request, allow-use-union mode, 4 rows with an extra column) is the load-bearing evidence, because without it a maintainer can say the answer WAS the union. Include it. Ask for 401 for consistency with the other branch, or a documented statement that __union__ degrades under default mode. Label vocabulary check: the 40 most recent nocobase/nocobase issues carry ZERO labels, so maintainers here rarely label outside triage. The labels suggested are real repo labels (verified via gh api repos/nocobase/nocobase/labels), but a Suggested labels line will probably go unused. The only issue template is bug_report.md with sections: Describe the bug, Environment, How To Reproduce, Expected behavior, Screenshots, Logs. No template-enforcing workflow was detected, but match the sections anyway.
